As far as diet goes, If you eat until you are 80% full and you're still 20lbs overweight then it's your sense of hunger which is wrong. This is actually pretty common. Hunger is a pretty primitive and dumb thing, and it will always strive to make you eat more, even when you don't need to eat more. Many animals will even eat themselves to death (Such as dogs), but humans have more control than that. If you habitually over-eat, your hunger will continue to tell you to over-eat, it's a case of your body not knowing what is best for it. I used to drink a tonne of coke (or similar fizzy drinks) a day, like at least 1 litre, usually 2 or more, I also used to have 3 teaspoons of sugar in every hot drink I drank, which as a brit, is a LOT. I would binge eat crisps, chocolate and other sweets but often miss meals due to my binge eating. When drinking alcohol I'd use coca cola/pepsi etc for mixer too.

Now I only drink water and hot drinks without any sugar whatsoever, I also don't drink fruit juices because raw fruit is a lot more healthy due to the fiber, which i'll talk about later. I don't eat junk foods, crisps, sweets etc, I eat fruit and veg instead of that (I still have a sweet tooth, but grapes, satsumas, apples, bananas, kiwifruit, pomegranates etc etc fill that void really well and a lot more healthily). I don't miss out on meals anymore, and I cook my own food, because home cooked 400-800 calorie meals are much more filling than take-away food. 1 and a half slices of pizza or a full dinner plate of chicken and veg stir fry with black bean sauce and noodles... I know which one is going to fill me more lol.

I was talking to my friend about the benefits of a high fiber diet... Fiber is not something your body can process into calories, it's just roughage that passes through your digestive system, however it still fills you and it makes your gut work much more efficiently. Replacing a quarter of your meal with fiber is going to reduce it's calories significantly, but the meal will be just as, if not even more filling than it was before, it's going to take your body more energy to digest the food and it will be great for you. this is how 22 of the 500 calories in my stir fry come from the vegetables, yet the vegetables account for a third of the weight of the stir fry. Also with alcohol I'll drink soda water, which reduces the calories ridiculously.

Simple and easy changes to my diet make it stupidly easy to lose weight, without even trying.
